_about: LightManifestExample.json - a catalogue of every level face in Alien Trilogy that
carries a light or an animation. Generated by ALTEngine's one-shot LevelLightScanner
and kept here as a reference for anyone replacing the level models.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A replacement level model is just geometry: it carries no light
records and no animator bindings, so every blinking light, every wall panel that
changes state and every shaded surface would render flat unless the replacement says
what each face should be bound to. This file is the list of what the original bound
where, so a replacement can reproduce it.
HOW TO USE IT. In your .obj, tag faces with the two custom statements ALTEngine's OBJ
loader understands. Both apply to every face declared after them, like usemtl, and -1
clears them:
alt_light <0-127>   bind the face to that level light record
alt_anim  <n>       make the face animated, driven by animator ordinal n
The lightId values below drop straight into alt_light, and animatorOrdinal into
alt_anim. You are NOT limited to the counts here - use as many faces as you like on
one light or animator, and add faces the original never had.
FACE IDENTITY. Faces are listed as their vertex indices into the original .MAP, in
the order the .MAP stores them, with -1 in the fourth slot for a triangle. They are
here so you can find which surface in the original had which binding - they are not
how a replacement is matched, since your model has its own vertices.
WHAT IS LISTED. Only faces that are animated (drawRoutine 8) or whose light record is
non-static. Every face in the game has a light id, so listing them all would just be
the whole level; an ordinary static face needs nothing beyond flat lighting.
drawRoutine is the on-disk +0x12 byte: 0 and 2 are quads, 1 and 3 are triangles, 8
means animated. For routine 8 the original stored the ANIMATOR ORDINAL in the
texIndex field rather than a texture, which is why those groups list animatorOrdinal
instead.
lightMode is the record's behaviour: static, blink, blinkAlt (a second blink variant),
gouraud (per-corner colour), or unknown for a mode value we have not identified yet.
A blink record does nothing until a script arms it - see ToggleLight.

_summary.note: L361LEV.MAP is absent - LevelManifest.json flags the SECT12/SECT22/SECT32 folder names as inferred guesses, so that one is most likely in a different folder or under a different name.
